    54→## Recommended Testing Setup (for future implementation)
    55→
    56→### Philosophy
    57→
    58→CipherBox shall employ a **Test Pyramid** approach with comprehensive coverage at all layers. Backend and TEE development **must** follow **Test-Driven Development (TDD)**, while frontend relies on **End-to-End automation** for validation.
    59→
    60→**Core Principles:**
    61→- TDD is mandatory for all backend and TEE code - write tests first, then implementation
    62→- Test Pyramid structure: more unit tests, fewer E2E tests for fast feedback loops
    63→- All tests must run in CI/CD pipeline - no manual testing gates
    64→- Cryptographic operations require exhaustive testing with 100% coverage
    65→- Frontend coverage achieved through automated E2E browser tests (no TDD required)
    66→
    67→### Test Pyramid Structure
    68→
    69→**Target Ratios:**
    70→- Unit Tests: 70% of test suite
    71→- Integration Tests: 20% of test suite
    72→- E2E Tests: 10% of test suite
    73→
    74→**Layer Definitions:**
    75→
    76→| Layer | Scope | Speed | Dependencies |
    77→|-------|-------|-------|--------------|
    78→| Unit | Single function/class | < 5ms | All mocked |
    79→| Integration | Service composition, DB | 50-500ms | Real database, mocked externals |
    80→| API E2E | Full backend stack | 100ms-2s | Full app, mocked IPFS |
    81→| Frontend E2E | Complete application | 2-30s | Full stack |
    82→
    83→### Test Execution Environments
    84→
    85→**Unit Tests:**
    86→- Run on: Developer machines, CI runners
    87→- Dependencies: All mocked (database, IPFS, external APIs)
    88→- Database: None (mocked)
    89→- Secrets: None required
    90→- Parallelization: Full parallel execution
    91→
    92→**Integration Tests:**
    93→- Run on: Developer machines (Docker), CI runners
    94→- Dependencies: Real PostgreSQL in Docker, mocked IPFS/Pinata
    95→- Database: Test database with migrations, truncated between test suites
    96→- Secrets: Test credentials only (never production)
    97→- Parallelization: Sequential due to shared database state
    98→
    99→**API E2E Tests:**
   100→- Run on: Developer machines, CI runners, optionally staging
   101→- Dependencies: Full NestJS application, real database, mocked IPFS
   102→- Database: Test database, reset between test suites
   103→- Secrets: Test JWT keys, mock Web3Auth tokens
   104→
   105→**Frontend E2E Tests (Cypress/Puppeteer):**
   106→- Run on: Developer machines, CI runners, **staging environment**
   107→- Dependencies: Frontend app + Backend API + Database (full stack)
   108→- Database: Seeded with test fixtures, reset to snapshot between spec files
   109→- Browsers: Chrome (primary), Firefox, Edge
   110→- Parallelization: Parallel specs via Cypress Cloud
   111→
   112→**TEE Tests:**
   113→- Local/CI: Mock enclave, attestation skipped, test keys
   114→- Staging: Real Phala testnet enclave, attestation verified, test keys (not production)
   115→
   116→### Framework Requirements
   117→
   118→*Note: This section specifies framework choices and requirements. Concrete configuration files and implementation examples will be created when the testing infrastructure is implemented.*
   119→
   120→**Backend (NestJS):**
   121→- Test Runner: Jest (NestJS default)
   122→- Mocking: `@nestjs/testing` module with Jest mocks
   123→- HTTP Testing: Supertest for API endpoint testing
   124→- Coverage: Jest/Istanbul with enforced thresholds
   125→
   126→**Frontend (React):**
   127→- E2E Framework: Cypress (recommended) or Puppeteer
   128→- Component Testing: Cypress Component Testing for complex components (optional)
   129→- Visual Regression: Percy integration (optional)
   130→
   131→**TEE (Rust):**
   132→- Test Framework: Native Rust `#[test]` attributes
   133→- Integration: Custom mock enclave harness for local testing
   134→
   135→### TDD Requirements (Backend & TEE)
   136→
   137→**Mandatory Workflow - Red-Green-Refactor:**
   138→1. RED: Write a failing test for new functionality
   139→2. GREEN: Write minimal code to make the test pass
   140→3. REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests green
   141→4. COMMIT: After each green phase
   142→5. REPEAT: Next requirement
   143→
   144→**TDD Rules:**
   145→- No production code without a failing test first
   146→- Tests must fail for the right reason before implementing
   147→- Write the simplest code to pass the test
   148→- Refactor only when tests are green
   149→
   150→**What Backend Unit Tests Must Cover:**
   151→- Service methods in isolation
   152→- Controller request handling and response formatting
   153→- DTOs and validation logic
   154→- Utility functions (crypto, data conversion)
   155→- Guards and middleware
   156→- Error handling and edge cases
   157→
   158→### Frontend E2E Requirements
   159→
   160→**No TDD required** - coverage achieved through comprehensive browser automation.
   161→
   162→**Test Coverage Must Include:**
   163→- All critical user journeys (authentication, file upload/download, folder operations)
   164→- Error scenarios and recovery flows
   165→- Cross-browser compatibility (Chrome, Firefox, Edge)
   166→
   167→**Selector Strategy:**
   168→- Use `data-testid` attributes exclusively for test selectors
   169→- Avoid flaky selectors (timing-based, nth-child, CSS classes)
   170→
   171→**Test Organization:**
   172→- Group by feature area: `auth/`, `vault/`, `settings/`
   173→- Separate spec files per user journey
   174→- Shared fixtures for mock data and responses
   175→- Custom commands for common operations (login, createVault, uploadFile)
   176→
   177→### Coverage Requirements
   178→
   179→**Backend Coverage Thresholds:**
   180→
   181→| Area | Line Coverage | Branch Coverage |
   182→|------|---------------|-----------------|
   183→| Crypto Services | 100% | 100% |
   184→| Auth Services | 90% | 85% |
   185→| Vault Services | 90% | 85% |
   186→| IPFS/IPNS Services | 85% | 80% |
   187→| Controllers | 80% | 75% |
   188→| Guards/Middleware | 90% | 85% |
   189→| **Overall Minimum** | **85%** | **80%** |
   190→
   191→**TEE Coverage Thresholds:**
   192→
   193→| Area | Coverage |
   194→|------|----------|
   195→| Crypto Functions | 100% |
   196→| Key Handling | 100% |
   197→| Error Paths | 100% |
   198→
   199→**Frontend E2E Metrics:**
   200→
   201→| Metric | Target |
   202→|--------|--------|
   203→| Critical User Journeys Covered | 100% |
   204→| Error Scenarios Tested | 90% |
   205→| Test Pass Rate | 100% |
   206→| Flaky Tests | 0% |
   207→
   208→### Mocking Guidelines
   209→
   210→**What to Mock:**
   211→- Database connections and queries (unit tests only)
   212→- IPFS client operations (network calls)
   213→- Pinata API calls
   214→- Web3Auth verification
   215→- External HTTP services
   216→
   217→**What NOT to Mock:**
   218→- Cryptographic functions - always test real encryption/decryption
   219→- Data conversion utilities (hexToBytes, bytesToHex)
   220→- Validation logic
   221→
   222→### Automated Linting & Pre-commit Hooks
   223→
   224→**Pre-commit Hook Requirements:**
   225→- ESLint with `--max-warnings 0` (zero tolerance for lint errors)
   226→- Prettier formatting check
   227→- TypeScript type checking
   228→- Unit tests for changed files only (`jest --findRelatedTests`)
   229→- Cargo fmt and Clippy for Rust code
   230→
   231→**Pre-push Hook Requirements:**
   232→- Full unit test suite
   233→- Integration tests
   234→- Coverage threshold verification
   235→- Build verification
   236→
   237→**Enforcement:**
   238→- Commits blocked if any check fails
   239→- No `eslint-disable` comments without PR justification
   240→- No `.skip()` or `.only()` in tests (enforced via ESLint rules)
   241→- Bypassing hooks (`--no-verify`) requires explicit justification in PR
   242→
   243→**CI Duplication:**
   244→- All pre-commit checks duplicated in CI pipeline
   245→- Catches bypassed hooks - bypassing locally only delays failure
   246→
   247→### CI Pipeline Structure
   248→
   249→**Stage 1: Lint & Type Check (parallel)**
   250→- ESLint (Backend + Frontend)
   251→- Prettier formatting verification
   252→- TypeScript compilation check
   253→- Cargo fmt + Clippy (TEE)
   254→
   255→**Stage 2: Unit Tests (parallel, no services needed)**
   256→- Backend unit tests with coverage
   257→- TEE unit tests with coverage
   258→- Coverage threshold enforcement
   259→
   260→**Stage 3: Integration Tests**
   261→- Backend integration tests
   262→- Requires PostgreSQL service container
   263→
   264→**Stage 4: E2E Tests (parallel)**
   265→- API E2E tests (full backend + database)
   266→- Frontend Cypress tests (full stack)
   267→- Screenshot/video artifacts on failure
   268→
   269→**Stage 5: Build & Deploy**
   270→- Production build verification
   271→- Deploy to staging (main branch only)
   272→
   273→### Test Data Management
   274→
   275→**Data Lifecycle by Test Level:**
   276→
   277→| Level | Setup | Cleanup | Isolation |
   278→|-------|-------|---------|-----------|
   279→| Unit | In-memory mocks | Automatic (GC) | Per test |
   280→| Integration | Migrations + seeds | Truncate tables | Per suite |
   281→| API E2E | Fixtures via API | Truncate tables | Per suite |
   282→| Frontend E2E | Seeded database | Reset to snapshot | Per spec file |
   283→
   284→**Fixture Requirements:**
   285→- Factory functions for test entities (users, vaults, files)
   286→- Deterministic test keys for reproducible crypto tests
   287→- JSON fixtures for Cypress mock responses
   288→
   289→### Priority Test Areas
   290→
   291→Based on project criticality:
   292→
   293→1. **Cryptographic correctness** (highest priority)
   294→   - Encryption/decryption roundtrips must always pass
   295→   - Key derivation consistency
   296→   - ECIES key wrapping integrity
   297→   - Tamper detection (modified ciphertext, wrong keys)
   298→
   299→2. **Authentication & Authorization**
   300→   - Token validation and expiry
   301→   - Permission boundaries
   302→   - Session management
   303→
   304→3. **Data Integrity**
   305→   - Metadata encryption/decryption
   306→   - File content verification
   307→   - IPNS record signing
   308→
   309→4. **User Journeys (E2E)**
   310→   - Login → Create Vault → Upload File → Download File → Logout
   311→   - Folder creation and navigation
   312→   - Multi-device sync across devices
   313→

1→import { create } from 'zustand';
     2→
     3→type SyncStatus = 'idle' | 'syncing' | 'success' | 'error';
     4→
     5→type SyncState = {
     6→  // Sync status
     7→  status: SyncStatus;
     8→  lastSyncTime: Date | null;
     9→  syncError: string | null;
    10→
    11→  // Initial sync tracking
    12→  initialSyncComplete: boolean;
    13→
    14→  // Network status
    15→  isOnline: boolean;
    16→
    17→  // Actions
    18→  startSync: () => void;
    19→  syncSuccess: () => void;
    20→  syncFailure: (error: string) => void;
    21→  completeInitialSync: () => void;
    22→  setOnline: (online: boolean) => void;
    23→  reset: () => void;
    24→};
    25→
    26→/**
    27→ * Sync state store for multi-device sync.
    28→ *
    29→ * Tracks:
    30→ * - Sync status (idle/syncing/success/error)
    31→ * - Last sync timestamp
    32→ * - Sync errors
    33→ * - Network online status
    34→ *
    35→ * Used by useSyncPolling hook and SyncIndicator component.
    36→ */
    37→export const useSyncStore = create<SyncState>((set) => ({
    38→  // Initial state
    39→  status: 'idle',
    40→  lastSyncTime: null,
    41→  syncError: null,
    42→  initialSyncComplete: false,
    43→  isOnline: typeof navigator !== 'undefined' ? navigator.onLine : true,
    44→
    45→  // Actions
    46→  startSync: () =>
    47→    set({
    48→      status: 'syncing',
    49→      syncError: null,
    50→    }),
    51→
    52→  syncSuccess: () =>
    53→    set({
    54→      status: 'success',
    55→      lastSyncTime: new Date(),
    56→      syncError: null,
    57→    }),
    58→
    59→  syncFailure: (error) =>
    60→    set({
    61→      status: 'error',
    62→      syncError: error,
    63→    }),
    64→
    65→  completeInitialSync: () => set({ initialSyncComplete: true }),
    66→
    67→  setOnline: (online) => set({ isOnline: online }),
    68→
    69→  reset: () =>
    70→    set({
    71→      status: 'idle',
    72→      lastSyncTime: null,
    73→      syncError: null,
    74→      initialSyncComplete: false,
    75→    }),
    76→}));

    38→  @Throttle({ default: { limit: 10, ttl: 60000 } }) // 10 publishes per minute per user

    57→    status: 401,
    58→    description: 'Unauthorized - JWT token required',

- Milestone 2: Production v1.0 (Phases 11-17) -- in progress
- Milestone 3: Encrypted Productivity Suite (Phases 18-21) -- planned

## Phases

**Phase Numbering:**

- Integer phases (1, 2, 3): Planned milestone work
- Decimal phases (2.1, 2.2): Urgent insertions (marked with INSERTED)

Decimal phases appear between their surrounding integers in numeric order.

1. Client detects when another device has published a newer IPNS sequence number and alerts the user before overwriting
2. On conflict, both web and desktop clients automatically re-sync the folder and retry the operation once
3. Persistent conflicts (retry also fails) surface an error to the user without infinite loops

**Plans:** 3 plans

Plans:

- [ ] 16-01-PLAN.md — API: expectedSequenceNumber on publish DTOs, conflict check in upsertFolderIpns, batch folder-first validation, 409 response, unit tests
- [ ] 16-02-PLAN.md — Web client: API client regen, expectedSequenceNumber in folder publish paths, 409 handling with re-sync + retry in mutation hooks, sync store conflict status, SyncIndicator conflict state
- [ ] 16-03-PLAN.md — Desktop client: expected_sequence_number in IpnsPublishRequest, PublishResult enum, conflict handling in spawn_metadata_publish with re-sync + retry

### Phase 17: AWS Nitro TEE

**Goal**: IPNS republishing has a fallback TEE provider for high availability
**Depends on**: Phase 12 (can run in parallel with Phases 14-16 after MFA stabilizes auth)
**Requirements**: TEE-06
**Research flag**: NEEDS `/gsd:research-phase` -- Rust enclave binary, vsock communication, KMS attestation are entirely new technology for this project. Highest-risk item in M2.
**Success Criteria** (what must be TRUE):

1. AWS Nitro enclave can receive ECIES-encrypted IPNS keys, decrypt in hardware, sign IPNS records, and zero memory
2. Backend routes republish jobs to Nitro when Phala Cloud is unavailable, with automatic failover and failback
   **Plans**: TBD

## Progress

**Execution Order:**

Sequential order: 12 -> 12.5 -> 12.6 -> 12.1 -> 11.2 -> 13 -> 14 -> 15 -> 15.1 -> 16 -> 17 -> 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21

Parallel phases:

- Phase 11 (Windows Desktop) can run in parallel with any M2 phase (depends only on Phase 9/M1).
- Phase 11.3 (Linux Desktop) can run in parallel with any M2 phase (depends on Phase 11 for platform abstraction).

## PLANNING COMPLETE

**Phase:** 16-advanced-sync (Conflict Detection)
**Plans:** 3 plans in 2 waves

### Wave Structure

| Wave | Plans | Autonomous |
|------|-------|------------|
| 1 | 16-01 (API) | yes |
| 2 | 16-02 (Web), 16-03 (Desktop) | yes, yes |

### Plans Created

| Plan | Objective | Tasks | Key Files |
|------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| 16-01 | API optimistic concurrency: expectedSequenceNumber on publish DTOs, conflict check in upsertFolderIpns, batch folder-first validation, 409 response, unit tests | 2 | `apps/api/src/ipns/dto/publish.dto.ts`, `ipns.service.ts`, `ipns.controller.ts`, `ipns.service.spec.ts` |
| 16-02 | Web client: API client regen, expectedSequenceNumber in folder publish paths, 409 handling with re-sync + retry in mutation hooks, sync store conflict status, SyncIndicator conflict state | 2 | `apps/web/src/services/ipns.service.ts`, `folder.service.ts`, `useFolderMutations.ts`, `useFileOperations.ts`, `sync.store.ts`, `SyncIndicator.tsx`, `errors.ts` |
| 16-03 | Desktop client: expected_sequence_number in IpnsPublishRequest, PublishResult enum, conflict handling in spawn_metadata_publish with re-sync + retry | 2 | `apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/api/ipns.rs`, `fuse/mod.rs` |

### Key Design Decisions

- **Scope rescoped:** Offline queue (SYNC-05) and idempotent replay (SYNC-06) deferred to Milestone 3 per CONTEXT.md
- **Folder-only conflict detection:** Per-file IPNS uses last-write-wins; versioning (Phase 13) is the safety net
- **Single retry with jitter:** On conflict, re-sync + retry once. Persistent conflict surfaces error. No infinite loops
- **Backward compatible:** `expectedSequenceNumber` is optional. Absent = unconditional publish (TEE republish, per-file publishes, old clients)
- **Batch conflict strategy:** If any folder record in a batch conflicts, the entire batch fails with 409 (file records are useless without the folder record)

1→# Phase 16: Advanced Sync (Conflict Detection) - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-03-03
     4→**Domain:** IPNS publish conflict detection via optimistic concurrency
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 16 adds conflict detection to IPNS folder publishes using API-level optimistic concurrency. The mechanism is: clients send their expected sequence number with each publish request; the API compares it against the stored value in `folder_ipns` and rejects mismatches. On rejection, the client re-syncs and retries.
    10→
    11→The codebase is well-positioned for this change. The `folder_ipns` table already tracks `sequence_number` (bigint), the publish endpoint already returns the new sequence number, and both clients already track sequence numbers locally. The key work is: (1) adding an `expectedSequenceNumber` field to publish DTOs, (2) checking it in `upsertFolderIpns`, (3) returning a 409 Conflict response, and (4) handling that response on both web and desktop clients with re-sync + retry logic.
    12→
    13→**Primary recommendation:** Add a single `expectedSequenceNumber` optional field to the publish DTO. When present, the API validates it against the stored value. When absent (backward compatibility for per-file publishes), no check is performed. Return HTTP 409 with a body containing the current server sequence number so the client knows how far behind it is.
    14→
    15→## Current Architecture
    16→
    17→### How IPNS Publish Works Today
    18→
    19→**Publish Flow (both clients):**
    20→
    21→1. Client modifies folder state locally (add/remove/rename child)
    22→2. Client encrypts updated folder metadata with folder key (AES-256-GCM)
    23→3. Client uploads encrypted metadata blob to IPFS (gets CID back)
    24→4. Client creates IPNS record: signs `value=/ipfs/{CID}` with Ed25519 key, increments local sequence number
    25→5. Client calls `POST /ipns/publish` (or `POST /ipns/publish-batch`) with: ipnsName, base64 record, metadataCid
    26→6. API's `upsertFolderIpns` increments the DB sequence number and stores new CID
    27→7. API relays the signed IPNS record to delegated-ipfs.dev (best-effort)
    28→8. API returns `{ success, ipnsName, sequenceNumber }`
    29→
    30→**Critical observation:** The API currently increments `sequenceNumber` unconditionally on every publish. There is NO check that the client's sequence number matches the server's. Two devices publishing simultaneously will both succeed, and the second will silently overwrite the first's metadata CID.
    31→
    32→### Sequence Number Management
    33→
    34→**API side (`upsertFolderIpns` in `ipns.service.ts` lines 158-239):**
    35→
    36→- On existing record: `sequenceNumber = BigInt(existing.sequenceNumber) + 1n`
    37→- On new record: `sequenceNumber = '0'`
    38→- No comparison with any client-provided value
    39→
    40→**Web client (`folder.service.ts`):**
    41→
    42→- Each `FolderNode` stores `sequenceNumber: bigint` in the Zustand store
    43→- On load: sequence comes from `resolveIpnsRecord` response
    44→- On publish: local sequence is incremented before IPNS record creation (`newSeq = params.sequenceNumber + 1n`)
    45→- The API response's `sequenceNumber` is stored back via `updateFolderSequence`
    46→- **Gap:** The local sequence in the IPNS record body and the API's DB sequence can diverge if two devices publish concurrently
    47→
    48→**Desktop client (`PublishCoordinator` in `fuse/mod.rs` lines 123-209):**
    49→
    50→- `seq_cache: HashMap<String, u64>` -- monotonic (only increases)
    51→- `resolve_sequence()` calls `resolve_ipns` API, returns `max(resolved, cached)`
    52→- `record_publish()` updates cache after successful publish
    53→- Per-folder publish locks prevent concurrent local publishes
    54→- **Gap:** The sequence resolved from the API reflects remote state, but another device could publish between resolve and publish
    55→
    56→### The folder_ipns Table
    57→
    58→```
    59→folder_ipns

    62→user_id                   uuid FK -> users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

    64→latest_cid                varchar(255) nullable -- current metadata CID

   135→## Web Client Publish Flow
   136→
   137→### Where Folder Publishes Happen
   138→
   139→Every folder mutation flows through `updateFolderMetadata` in `folder.service.ts`:
   140→
   141→```typescript
   142→export async function updateFolderMetadata(params: {
   143→  folderId: string;
   144→  children: FolderChild[];
   145→  folderKey: Uint8Array;
   146→  ipnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array;
   147→  ipnsName: string;
   148→  sequenceNumber: bigint; // <-- current known sequence
   149→  encryptedIpnsPrivateKey?: string;
   150→  keyEpoch?: number;
   151→}): Promise<{ cid: string; newSequenceNumber: bigint }>;
   152→```
   153→
   154→**Callers of `updateFolderMetadata` (i.e., all folder publish points):**
   155→
   156→1. `useFolderMutations.handleCreate` -- creates subfolder, publishes parent + new folder
   157→2. `useFolderMutations.handleRename` -- renames item, publishes parent via `renameFolder`/`renameFile`
   158→3. `useFolderMutations.handleMove` -- moves item, publishes source and destination
   159→4. `useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems` -- batch move, publishes dest then source
   160→5. `useFolderMutations.handleDelete` -- deletes item, publishes parent via `deleteFolder`/`deleteFileFromFolder`
   161→6. `useFolderMutations.handleDeleteItems` -- batch delete, publishes parent
   162→7. `useFileOperations.handleAddFile` -- uploads file, batch publishes file IPNS + folder via `addFileToFolder`
   163→8. `useFileOperations.handleAddFiles` -- multi-file upload, batch publishes all files + folder via `addFilesToFolder`
   164→9. `useFileOperations.handleUpdateFile` -- updates file content (publishes file IPNS only, NOT folder -- **no conflict check needed**)
   165→10. `checkAndRotateIfNeeded` -- lazy key rotation, publishes folder
   166→
   167→**Batch publish path (`addFileToFolder`, `addFilesToFolder`):**
   168→These use `buildFolderIpnsRecord` + `batchPublishIpnsRecords` instead of `updateFolderMetadata`. The folder record is one entry in the batch alongside file records. Conflict detection must also work here.
   169→
   170→### Sequence Number Tracking in Web Client
   171→
   172→The `FolderNode` in Zustand stores `sequenceNumber: bigint`. Updates:
   173→
   174→- On initial load: from `resolveIpnsRecord` response
   175→- On publish: `updateFolderSequence(parentId, newSequenceNumber)` after publish succeeds
   176→- On sync poll: `updateFolderSequence('root', resolved.sequenceNumber)` after detecting remote changes
   177→
   178→**Important:** Only the root folder is polled for remote changes during sync. Subfolder changes are detected indirectly (root metadata changes -> subfolder metadata is stale).
   179→
   180→## Desktop Client Publish Flow
   181→
   182→### Where Folder Publishes Happen
   183→
   184→Desktop FUSE mutations call `CipherBoxFS::update_folder_metadata(folder_ino)` which calls `spawn_metadata_publish`:
   185→
   186→```rust
   187→fn spawn_metadata_publish(
   188→    api: Arc<ApiClient>,
   189→    rt: tokio::runtime::Handle,
   190→    metadata: FolderMetadata,
   191→    folder_key: Vec<u8>,
   192→    ipns_private_key: Vec<u8>,
   193→    ipns_name: String,
   194→    old_metadata_cid: Option<String>,
   195→    coordinator: Arc<PublishCoordinator>,
   196→)
   197→```
   198→
   199→**Inside `spawn_metadata_publish`:**
   200→
   201→1. Acquire per-folder publish lock (`coordinator.get_lock`)
   202→2. Encrypt metadata (CPU-only)
   203→3. `coordinator.resolve_sequence(api, ipns_name)` -- gets current seq from API
   204→4. Upload encrypted metadata to IPFS
   205→5. Create IPNS record with `new_seq = seq + 1`
   206→6. Call `POST /ipns/publish`
   207→7. `coordinator.record_publish(ipns_name, new_seq)`
   208→
   209→**FUSE write operations that trigger folder publish:**
   210→
   211→- `handle_create` -- new file (via debounce queue)
   212→- `handle_unlink` -- delete file (immediate via `update_folder_metadata`)
   213→- `handle_mkdir` -- new folder (immediate, spawns background thread)
   214→- `handle_rmdir` -- delete folder (immediate via `update_folder_metadata`)
   215→- `handle_rename` -- rename/move (immediate via `update_folder_metadata`)
   216→- `release` -- file upload complete (via debounce queue)
   217→
   218→### PublishCoordinator Details
   219→
   220→```rust
   221→pub struct PublishCoordinator {
   222→    seq_cache: Mutex<HashMap<String, u64>>,      // monotonic local cache
   223→    publish_locks: Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>>, // per-IPNS serialize
   224→}
   225→```
   226→
   227→**`resolve_sequence` behavior:**
   228→
   229→- Calls `resolve_ipns` API -> gets remote seq
   230→- Returns `max(remote_seq, cached_seq)` -- prevents rollback
   231→- On resolve failure with cache hit: returns cached value (fallback)
   232→- On resolve failure without cache: returns error (prevents publishing with unknown seq)
   233→
   234→**The per-folder lock prevents concurrent local publishes** but does NOT prevent conflicts from another device publishing between resolve and publish. This is the exact gap that conflict detection fills.

   236→## Sync & Polling Mechanism
   237→
   238→### Web Client Sync
   239→
   240→**`useSyncPolling` hook (`useSyncPolling.ts`):**
   241→
   242→- 30s polling interval via `useInterval`
   243→- Pauses when tab is backgrounded or offline
   244→- Fires immediately on mount, visibility regain, and reconnect
   245→- Updates sync store status: idle -> syncing -> success/error
   246→
   247→**Sync callback (`FileBrowser.tsx` lines 116-164):**
   248→
   249→1. Resolve root IPNS name via `resolveIpnsRecord`
   250→2. Compare `resolved.sequenceNumber` with `rootFolder.sequenceNumber`
   251→3. If remote > local: fetch and decrypt new metadata, update store
   252→4. Only polls root folder -- subfolder sync is implicit (root metadata changes reference subfolders)
   253→
   254→**Extension point for conflict re-sync:** The sync callback can be triggered on-demand by calling `doSync()`. After a 409 conflict response, the client could call the sync logic and then retry the operation.
   255→
   256→### Desktop Client Sync
   257→
   258→**`SyncDaemon` (`sync/mod.rs`):**
   259→
   260→- 30s polling interval via tokio timer
   261→- `sync_now_rx` channel for manual triggers (tray "Sync Now" button)
   262→- `poll()`: resolves root IPNS, compares sequence numbers, logs changes
   263→- On change: metadata cache TTL (30s) handles refresh on next FUSE access
   264→- Tray status transitions: Syncing -> Synced / Offline / Error
   265→
   266→**Extension point for conflict re-sync:** The SyncDaemon's `sync_now_rx` channel can trigger immediate re-sync. On conflict, the FUSE publish thread could send to this channel.

   304→## Batch Operations
   305→
   306→### Multi-file Upload
   307→
   308→`addFilesToFolder` creates N file IPNS records + 1 folder IPNS record and sends them all in one `batchPublishIpnsRecords` call. The folder record is the one that needs conflict detection.
   309→
   310→**Important design question:** In a batch publish where individual records can fail independently, should a folder conflict fail the entire batch (preventing the file records from publishing too) or only fail the folder record?
   311→
   312→**Recommendation:** Fail the entire batch when a folder record has a conflict. Reason: the file IPNS records are pointless without the folder record succeeding, because the folder metadata is what makes the files discoverable. Publishing file records but failing the folder record creates orphaned file IPNS records.
   313→
   314→This means: for batch publishes containing a `recordType: 'folder'` entry with `expectedSequenceNumber`, validate the folder entry FIRST. If it conflicts, reject the whole batch with 409.
   315→
   316→### Move Operations
   317→
   318→`handleMove` and `handleMoveItems` publish to two folders sequentially (add-before-remove pattern). If the destination publish succeeds but the source publish conflicts:
   319→
   320→- The item appears in both folders temporarily
   321→- After re-sync, the client sees the conflict on the source folder
   322→- Retry: re-read source folder, remove item, re-publish
   323→- The add-before-remove pattern means data is safe (item exists in at least one folder)
   324→

   441→## Common Pitfalls
   442→
   443→### Pitfall 1: Race Between Resolve and Publish
   444→
   445→**What goes wrong:** Client resolves seq=5, another device publishes (seq becomes 6), client publishes with expectedSeq=5, gets 409.
   446→**Why it happens:** Normal multi-device usage. The resolve-then-publish pattern has an inherent TOCTOU window.
   447→**How to avoid:** This is expected behavior -- the conflict detection is designed to catch this. The client's response (re-sync + retry) handles it.
   448→
   449→### Pitfall 2: Stale Zustand Closures in Retry Logic
   450→
   451→**What goes wrong:** The retry callback uses the original `parentFolderState` from the closure, which has the stale sequence number and children.
   452→**Why it happens:** React hook callbacks capture state at render time.
   453→**How to avoid:** In retry logic, ALWAYS re-read from `useFolderStore.getState()` to get fresh folder state. This is a known pattern in this codebase (see MEMORY.md "Zustand stale closures in async callbacks").
   454→
   455→### Pitfall 3: Infinite Retry on Persistent Conflict
   456→
   457→**What goes wrong:** Two devices in a tight loop modifying the same folder cause infinite conflict retries.
   458→**Why it happens:** Each retry triggers a new publish which conflicts with the other device's retry.
   459→**How to avoid:** Limit to 1 retry per operation. If the retry also conflicts, surface an error to the user. Consider adding random jitter (100-500ms) before retry to break symmetry.
   460→
   461→### Pitfall 4: Batch Publish Partial Conflict
   462→
   463→**What goes wrong:** In a batch with 10 file records + 1 folder record, the folder conflicts but file records have already been processed.
   464→**Why it happens:** Current batch processing runs records concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.
   465→**How to avoid:** For batches containing a folder record with `expectedSequenceNumber`, validate the folder record FIRST. If it conflicts, return 409 for the entire batch before processing any records.
   466→
   467→### Pitfall 5: Move Operation Half-Conflict
   468→
   469→**What goes wrong:** Destination publish succeeds, source publish gets 409. Item exists in both folders.
   470→**Why it happens:** Move is two separate publish operations (add-before-remove).
   471→**How to avoid:** This is actually safe due to add-before-remove pattern. On source conflict: re-sync source folder, re-verify item is still in source children, re-publish removal. The item temporarily appears in both folders but data is not lost.
   472→
   473→### Pitfall 6: Desktop Publish Lock Does Not Prevent Remote Conflicts
   474→
   475→**What goes wrong:** Developer assumes `PublishCoordinator.get_lock` prevents all conflicts.
   476→**Why it happens:** The lock only serializes local publishes from the same desktop process.
   477→**How to avoid:** The lock is necessary (prevents local race conditions) but not sufficient (does not prevent remote device conflicts). Both the local lock AND the API-level conflict check are needed.
   478→
   479→### Pitfall 7: Conflict During Lazy Key Rotation
   480→
   481→**What goes wrong:** `checkAndRotateIfNeeded` publishes re-encrypted metadata, but another device published since the last sync.
   482→**Why it happens:** Key rotation resolves IPNS, re-encrypts, publishes -- standard TOCTOU window.
   483→**How to avoid:** Key rotation publish should also use `expectedSequenceNumber`. On conflict, re-sync, re-read metadata, and re-encrypt with the new key using the fresh children.
   484→
   485→## Don't Hand-Roll
   486→
   487→| Problem                     | Don't Build                | Use Instead                          | Why                                                                                     |
   488→| --------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   489→| Conflict detection protocol | Custom distributed locking | HTTP 409 + `expectedSequenceNumber`  | Standard optimistic concurrency pattern; proven at scale                                |
   490→| OS notifications on desktop | Custom notification system | `tauri-plugin-notification`          | Already a dependency, handles macOS/Windows/Linux                                       |
   491→| Web toast notifications     | Custom toast from scratch  | Simple CSS transition + `setTimeout` | The existing codebase uses inline components, not a toast library; keep it consistent   |
   492→| Retry backoff               | Custom exponential backoff | Single retry with random jitter      | Conflicts are rare (30s poll interval >> publish duration); complex backoff is overkill |

   573→## Risk Assessment
   574→
   575→### Low Risk
   576→
   577→- **API DTO change:** Adding an optional field is backward-compatible
   578→- **409 response code:** Standard HTTP semantics, well-understood
   579→- **Web toast notification:** Simple UI addition, no complex state
   580→
   581→### Medium Risk
   582→
   583→- **Batch publish conflict handling:** Need to restructure batch processing to validate folder records first. Current `Promise.allSettled` concurrent processing must be changed to sequential for folder records with conflict checks.
   584→- **Desktop conflict retry in FUSE context:** The FUSE callback thread spawns a background publish thread. On conflict, the retry must re-read inode state which may have changed. Need careful locking.
   585→- **Move operation half-conflict:** Safe due to add-before-remove, but the retry logic for the source removal needs to handle the case where the item was already removed by the other device's sync.
   586→
   587→### Low Probability but High Impact
   588→
   589→- **TypeORM race condition:** Two publish requests arriving simultaneously could both read the same `sequenceNumber` before either writes. Using a DB-level `WHERE sequence_number = expected` in the UPDATE query (instead of read-then-compare) would be more robust. Consider using TypeORM's query builder with a conditional update.
   590→
   591→## Open Questions
   592→
   593→1. **DB-level vs application-level check:**
   594→   - Current plan: read record, compare in TypeScript, then update
   595→   - More robust: `UPDATE folder_ipns SET sequence_number = seq + 1 WHERE sequence_number = expected RETURNING *`
   596→   - Recommendation: Use DB-level `WHERE` clause for atomicity. The application-level read-compare-write has a TOCTOU gap under high concurrency.
   597→   - **Confidence:** MEDIUM -- need to verify TypeORM supports conditional updates well
   598→
   599→2. **Should subfolder sync be added?**
   600→   - Currently only root folder is polled on web. If a conflict occurs on a subfolder, the client needs to re-sync that specific subfolder.
   601→   - Recommendation: On conflict, resolve the specific folder's IPNS (not just root), fetch and decrypt, update store. This is already how `loadFolder` works.
   602→   - **Confidence:** HIGH -- the resolve infrastructure exists
   603→
   604→3. **TEE republish interaction:**
   605→   - TEE republishes use `sequence_number` from the `republish_schedules` table. TEE does NOT use `expectedSequenceNumber`.
   606→   - Does a TEE republish increment the `folder_ipns.sequence_number`? Looking at the code, TEE publishes go through the same `upsertFolderIpns` path, which increments unconditionally.
   607→   - This means a TEE republish could cause a client conflict even though the content hasn't changed (same CID, just refreshed IPNS TTL).
   608→   - Recommendation: Only set `expectedSequenceNumber` on client publishes. TEE republishes continue without it. The DB sequence will still increment on TEE republish, but since TEE uses the same CID, the client's next sync will see a higher sequence number with identical content -- triggering a no-op refresh.
   609→   - **Confidence:** HIGH -- TEE publish path already uses the same upsert without expected seq

1→#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2→set -euo pipefail
     3→
     4→# test-round-trip.sh -- Verify desktop FUSE writes are visible via the API.
     5→#
     6→# Usage: ./test-round-trip.sh [mount-point] [api-url]
     7→#   mount-point  Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
     8→#   api-url      Backend API URL (default: http://localhost:3000)
     9→#
    10→# Environment:
    11→#   TEST_SECRET  Shared secret for test-login (default: e2e-test-secret-ci-only)
    12→#
    13→# The server is zero-knowledge -- it cannot decrypt file contents.
    14→# These tests prove the pipeline: FUSE write -> encrypt -> IPFS upload -> IPNS publish -> API visibility.
    15→#
    16→# Exit code: number of failed tests (0 = all passed).
    17→
    18→MP="${1:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
    19→API_URL="${2:-http://localhost:3000}"
    20→SECRET="${TEST_SECRET:-e2e-test-secret-ci-only}"
    21→# Use the same email as the dev-key auth flow so we query the same user's vault
    22→TEST_EMAIL="dev-key@cipherbox.local"
    23→
    24→PASS=0
    25→FAIL=0
    26→
    27→pass() {
    28→  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
    29→  echo "PASS: $1"
    30→}
    31→
    32→fail() {
    33→  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
    34→  echo "FAIL: $1"
    35→}
    36→
    37→echo "=== API Round-Trip Tests ==="
    38→echo "Mount point: $MP"
    39→echo "API URL:     $API_URL"
    40→echo "Test email:  $TEST_EMAIL"
    41→echo ""
    42→
    43→# ---- Test 1: Authenticate via test-login ----
    44→echo "--- Test 1: Authenticate via test-login ---"
    45→AUTH_RESPONSE=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 30 -X POST "$API_URL/auth/test-login" \
    46→  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    47→  -d "{\"email\":\"$TEST_EMAIL\",\"secret\":\"$SECRET\"}" 2>&1) || true
    48→
    49→ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.accessToken // empty')
    50→if [ -n "$ACCESS_TOKEN" ]; then
    51→  pass "Authenticate via test-login"
    52→else
    53→  AUTH_ERROR=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.message // .error // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "non-JSON response")
    54→  fail "Authenticate via test-login (error: $AUTH_ERROR)"
    55→  echo "FATAL: Cannot proceed without authentication."
    56→  echo ""
    57→  echo "=== API Round-Trip Results ==="
    58→  echo "  Passed: $PASS"
    59→  echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
    60→  echo "==============================="
    61→  exit "$FAIL"
    62→fi
    63→
    64→# ---- Test 2: Desktop writes file, API verifies vault exists ----
    65→echo "--- Test 2: Verify vault has content after FUSE write ---"
    66→echo "API-visible content" > "$MP/rt-test.txt"
    67→
    68→ROOT_IPNS=""

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# test-round-trip.sh -- Verify desktop FUSE writes are visible via the API.
#
# Usage: ./test-round-trip.sh [mount-point] [api-url]
#   mount-point  Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
#   api-url      Backend API URL (default: http://localhost:3000)
#
# Environment:
#   TEST_SECRET  Shared secret for test-login (default: e2e-test-secret-ci-only)
#
# The server is zero-knowledge -- it cannot decrypt file contents.
# These tests prove the pipeline: FUSE write -> encrypt -> IPFS upload -> IPNS publish -> API visibility.
#
# Exit code: number of failed tests (0 = all passed).

MP="${1:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
API_URL="${2:-http://localhost:3000}"
SECRET="${TEST_SECRET:-e2e-test-secret-ci-only}"
# Use the same email as the dev-key auth flow so we query the same user's vault
TEST_EMAIL="dev-key@cipherbox.local"

PASS=0
FAIL=0

pass() {
  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
  echo "PASS: $1"
}

fail() {
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  echo "FAIL: $1"
}

echo "=== API Round-Trip Tests ==="
echo "Mount point: $MP"
echo "API URL:     $API_URL"
echo "Test email:  $TEST_EMAIL"
echo ""

# ---- Test 1: Authenticate via test-login ----
echo "--- Test 1: Authenticate via test-login ---"
AUTH_RESPONSE=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 30 -X POST "$API_URL/auth/test-login" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"email\":\"$TEST_EMAIL\",\"secret\":\"$SECRET\"}" 2>&1) || true

ACCESS_TOKEN=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.accessToken // empty')
if [ -n "$ACCESS_TOKEN" ]; then
  pass "Authenticate via test-login"
else
  AUTH_ERROR=$(echo "$AUTH_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.message // .error // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "non-JSON response")
  fail "Authenticate via test-login (error: $AUTH_ERROR)"
  echo "FATAL: Cannot proceed without authentication."
  echo ""
  echo "=== API Round-Trip Results ==="
  echo "  Passed: $PASS"
  echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
  echo "==============================="
  exit "$FAIL"
fi

# ---- Test 2: Desktop writes file, API verifies vault exists ----
echo "--- Test 2: Verify vault has content after FUSE write ---"
echo "API-visible content" > "$MP/rt-test.txt"

ROOT_IPNS=""
for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
  sleep 5
  VAULT_RESPONSE=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
    "$API_URL/vault" 2>&1) || true
  ROOT_IPNS=$(echo "$VAULT_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.rootIpnsName // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  if [ -n "$ROOT_IPNS" ] && [ "$ROOT_IPNS" != "null" ]; then
    break
  fi
  echo "  Vault poll attempt $attempt: no rootIpnsName yet"
  ROOT_IPNS=""
done

if [ -n "$ROOT_IPNS" ] && [ "$ROOT_IPNS" != "null" ]; then
  pass "Vault has rootIpnsName after FUSE write ($ROOT_IPNS)"
else
  VAULT_ERROR=$(echo "$VAULT_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.message // .error // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "non-JSON response")
  fail "Vault has no rootIpnsName after 60s polling (error: $VAULT_ERROR)"
fi

# ---- Test 3: Verify IPNS resolve returns data ----
echo "--- Test 3: Verify IPNS resolve returns CID ---"
if [ -n "$ROOT_IPNS" ] && [ "$ROOT_IPNS" != "null" ]; then
  RESOLVED_CID=""
  for attempt in $(seq 1 12); do
    sleep 2
    IPNS_RESPONSE=$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 30 -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
      "$API_URL/ipns/resolve?ipnsName=$ROOT_IPNS" 2>&1) || true
    RESOLVED_CID=$(echo "$IPNS_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.cid // .value // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$RESOLVED_CID" ] && [ "$RESOLVED_CID" != "null" ]; then
      break
    fi
    echo "  IPNS resolve attempt $attempt: no CID yet"
    RESOLVED_CID=""
  done

  if [ -n "$RESOLVED_CID" ] && [ "$RESOLVED_CID" != "null" ]; then
    pass "IPNS resolve returned CID ($RESOLVED_CID)"
  else
    IPNS_ERROR=$(echo "$IPNS_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.message // .error // empty' 2>/dev/null || echo "non-JSON response")
    fail "IPNS resolve did not return expected CID after 24s polling (error: $IPNS_ERROR)"
  fi
else
  fail "IPNS resolve skipped (no rootIpnsName)"
fi

# ---- Cleanup ----
echo "--- Cleanup ---"
rm -f "$MP/rt-test.txt" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 2

# ---- Summary ----
echo ""
echo "=== API Round-Trip Results ==="
echo "  Passed: $PASS"
echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
echo "==============================="

exit "$FAIL"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

# test-fuse-operations.sh -- Exercise FUSE mount file I/O operations.
#
# Usage: ./test-fuse-operations.sh [mount-point]
#   mount-point  Path to FUSE mount (default: $HOME/CipherBox)
#
# Tests: create, read, overwrite, mkdir, nested write, binary round-trip,
#        rename, delete file, delete directory.
#
# Exit code: number of failed tests (0 = all passed).

MP="${1:-$HOME/CipherBox}"
PASS=0
FAIL=0

# Detect SHA-256 command (macOS vs Linux)
if command -v shasum &>/dev/null; then
  SHA256_CMD="shasum -a 256"
elif command -v sha256sum &>/dev/null; then
  SHA256_CMD="sha256sum"
else
  echo "FAIL: No SHA-256 command found (shasum or sha256sum)"
  exit 1
fi

pass() {
  PASS=$((PASS + 1))
  echo "PASS: $1"
}

fail() {
  FAIL=$((FAIL + 1))
  echo "FAIL: $1"
}

echo "=== FUSE File I/O Tests ==="
echo "Mount point: $MP"
echo ""

# ---- Test 1: Create and read text file ----
echo "--- Test 1: Create and read text file ---"
echo "Hello from CI" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"
sleep 3
CONTENT=$(cat "$MP/e2e-test.txt")
if [ "$CONTENT" = "Hello from CI" ]; then
  pass "Create and read text file"
else
  fail "Create and read text file (got: '$CONTENT')"
fi

# ---- Test 2: Create directory ----
echo "--- Test 2: Create directory ---"
mkdir -p "$MP/e2e-folder"
if [ -d "$MP/e2e-folder" ]; then
  pass "Create directory"
else
  fail "Create directory"
fi

# ---- Test 3: Write file in subdirectory ----
echo "--- Test 3: Write file in subdirectory ---"
echo "Nested content" > "$MP/e2e-folder/nested.txt"
sleep 3
NESTED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-folder/nested.txt")
if [ "$NESTED" = "Nested content" ]; then
  pass "Write file in subdirectory"
else
  fail "Write file in subdirectory (got: '$NESTED')"
fi

# ---- Test 4: Overwrite file (modify) ----
echo "--- Test 4: Overwrite file ---"
echo "Modified content" > "$MP/e2e-test.txt"
sleep 3
MODIFIED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-test.txt")
if [ "$MODIFIED" = "Modified content" ]; then
  pass "Overwrite file"
else
  fail "Overwrite file (got: '$MODIFIED')"
fi

# ---- Test 5: Binary file round-trip ----
echo "--- Test 5: Binary file round-trip ---"
dd if=/dev/urandom of=/tmp/e2e-binary.bin bs=1024 count=256 2>/dev/null
cp /tmp/e2e-binary.bin "$MP/e2e-binary.bin"
sleep 5
CHECKSUM_ORIG=$($SHA256_CMD /tmp/e2e-binary.bin | cut -d' ' -f1)
CHECKSUM_MOUNT=$($SHA256_CMD "$MP/e2e-binary.bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)
if [ "$CHECKSUM_ORIG" = "$CHECKSUM_MOUNT" ]; then
  pass "Binary file round-trip (256KB)"
else
  fail "Binary file round-trip (orig: $CHECKSUM_ORIG, mount: $CHECKSUM_MOUNT)"
fi

# ---- Test 6: Rename file ----
echo "--- Test 6: Rename file ---"
mv "$MP/e2e-test.txt" "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"
sleep 2
if [ ! -f "$MP/e2e-test.txt" ] && [ -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" ]; then
  RENAMED=$(cat "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt")
  if [ "$RENAMED" = "Modified content" ]; then
    pass "Rename file"
  else
    fail "Rename file (content changed: '$RENAMED')"
  fi
else
  fail "Rename file (old exists: $(test -f "$MP/e2e-test.txt" && echo yes || echo no), new exists: $(test -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" && echo yes || echo no))"
fi

# ---- Test 7: Delete file ----
echo "--- Test 7: Delete file ---"
rm "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt"
sleep 2
if [ ! -f "$MP/e2e-renamed.txt" ]; then
  pass "Delete file"
else
  fail "Delete file (still exists)"
fi

# ---- Test 8: Delete directory ----
echo "--- Test 8: Delete directory ---"
rm -rf "$MP/e2e-folder"
sleep 2
if [ ! -d "$MP/e2e-folder" ]; then
  pass "Delete directory"
else
  fail "Delete directory (still exists)"
fi

# ---- Test 9: Cleanup ----
echo "--- Test 9: Cleanup ---"
rm -f "$MP/e2e-binary.bin" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f /tmp/e2e-binary.bin 2>/dev/null || true
# Filter .DS_Store from any remaining file checks
REMAINING=$(ls "$MP" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '\.DS_Store' | grep -v '^$' || true)
if [ -z "$REMAINING" ]; then
  pass "Cleanup (mount point clean)"
else
  # Not a hard failure -- other files may be present from the desktop app
  pass "Cleanup (remaining files: $REMAINING)"
fi

# ---- Summary ----
echo ""
echo "=== FUSE File I/O Results ==="
echo "  Passed: $PASS"
echo "  Failed: $FAIL"
echo "=============================="

exit "$FAIL"

1→# Phase 16: Advanced Sync (Conflict Detection) - Research
     2→
     3→**Researched:** 2026-03-03
     4→**Domain:** IPNS publish conflict detection via optimistic concurrency
     5→**Confidence:** HIGH
     6→
     7→## Summary
     8→
     9→Phase 16 adds conflict detection to IPNS folder publishes using API-level optimistic concurrency. The mechanism is: clients send their expected sequence number with each publish request; the API compares it against the stored value in `folder_ipns` and rejects mismatches. On rejection, the client re-syncs and retries.
    10→
    11→The codebase is well-positioned for this change. The `folder_ipns` table already tracks `sequence_number` (bigint), the publish endpoint already returns the new sequence number, and both clients already track sequence numbers locally. The key work is: (1) adding an `expectedSequenceNumber` field to publish DTOs, (2) checking it in `upsertFolderIpns`, (3) returning a 409 Conflict response, and (4) handling that response on both web and desktop clients with re-sync + retry logic.
    12→
    13→**Primary recommendation:** Add a single `expectedSequenceNumber` optional field to the publish DTO. When present, the API validates it against the stored value. When absent (backward compatibility for per-file publishes), no check is performed. Return HTTP 409 with a body containing the current server sequence number so the client knows how far behind it is.
    14→
    15→## Current Architecture
    16→
    17→### How IPNS Publish Works Today
    18→
    19→**Publish Flow (both clients):**
    20→
    21→1. Client modifies folder state locally (add/remove/rename child)
    22→2. Client encrypts updated folder metadata with folder key (AES-256-GCM)
    23→3. Client uploads encrypted metadata blob to IPFS (gets CID back)
    24→4. Client creates IPNS record: signs `value=/ipfs/{CID}` with Ed25519 key, increments local sequence number
    25→5. Client calls `POST /ipns/publish` (or `POST /ipns/publish-batch`) with: ipnsName, base64 record, metadataCid
    26→6. API's `upsertFolderIpns` increments the DB sequence number and stores new CID
    27→7. API relays the signed IPNS record to delegated-ipfs.dev (best-effort)
    28→8. API returns `{ success, ipnsName, sequenceNumber }`
    29→
    30→**Critical observation:** The API currently increments `sequenceNumber` unconditionally on every publish. There is NO check that the client's sequence number matches the server's. Two devices publishing simultaneously will both succeed, and the second will silently overwrite the first's metadata CID.
    31→
    32→### Sequence Number Management
    33→
    34→**API side (`upsertFolderIpns` in `ipns.service.ts` lines 158-239):**
    35→
    36→- On existing record: `sequenceNumber = BigInt(existing.sequenceNumber) + 1n`
    37→- On new record: `sequenceNumber = '0'`
    38→- No comparison with any client-provided value
    39→
    40→**Web client (`folder.service.ts`):**
    41→
    42→- Each `FolderNode` stores `sequenceNumber: bigint` in the Zustand store
    43→- On load: sequence comes from `resolveIpnsRecord` response
    44→- On publish: local sequence is incremented before IPNS record creation (`newSeq = params.sequenceNumber + 1n`)
    45→- The API response's `sequenceNumber` is stored back via `updateFolderSequence`
    46→- **Gap:** The local sequence in the IPNS record body and the API's DB sequence can diverge if two devices publish concurrently
    47→
    48→**Desktop client (`PublishCoordinator` in `fuse/mod.rs` lines 123-209):**
    49→
    50→- `seq_cache: HashMap<String, u64>` -- monotonic (only increases)
    51→- `resolve_sequence()` calls `resolve_ipns` API, returns `max(resolved, cached)`
    52→- `record_publish()` updates cache after successful publish
    53→- Per-folder publish locks prevent concurrent local publishes
    54→- **Gap:** The sequence resolved from the API reflects remote state, but another device could publish between resolve and publish
    55→
    56→### The folder_ipns Table
    57→
    58→```
    59→folder_ipns
    60→-----------
    61→id                        uuid PK
    62→user_id                   uuid FK -> users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
    63→ipns_name                 varchar(255) -- IPNS name (k51... format)
    64→latest_cid                varchar(255) nullable -- current metadata CID
    65→sequence_number           bigint default 0 -- incremented on each publish
    66→encrypted_ipns_private_key bytea nullable -- ECIES-wrapped for TEE
    67→key_epoch                 int nullable -- TEE key rotation epoch
    68→is_root                   boolean default false
    69→record_type               varchar(10) default 'folder' -- 'folder' or 'file'
    70→created_at                timestamp
    71→updated_at                timestamp
    72→
    73→UNIQUE(user_id, ipns_name)
    74→INDEX(user_id)
    75→```
    76→
    77→**Key fields for conflict detection:**
    78→
    79→- `sequence_number` -- the authoritative server-side counter, always incremented by the API
    80→- `record_type` -- enables filtering: conflict checks apply only to `'folder'` records (per CONTEXT.md decision)
    81→
    82→## Publish Endpoints
    83→
    84→### POST /ipns/publish (single)
    85→
    86→**Current DTO (`PublishIpnsDto`):**
    87→
    88→```typescript
    89→{
    90→  ipnsName: string;         // k51... IPNS name
    91→  record: string;           // base64 IPNS record
    92→  metadataCid: string;      // CID of encrypted metadata
    93→  encryptedIpnsPrivateKey?: string; // hex, for TEE
    94→  keyEpoch?: number;
    95→}
    96→```
    97→
    98→**Current Response (`PublishIpnsResponseDto`):**
    99→
   100→```typescript
   101→{
   102→  success: boolean;
   103→  ipnsName: string;
   104→  sequenceNumber: string; // new seq as string
   105→}
   106→```
   107→
   108→### POST /ipns/publish-batch
   109→
   110→**Current DTO (`BatchPublishIpnsDto`):**
   111→
   112→```typescript
   113→{
   114→  records: PublishIpnsEntryDto[]; // max 200
   115→}
   116→```
   117→
   118→Each `PublishIpnsEntryDto` has same fields as `PublishIpnsDto` plus optional `recordType: 'folder' | 'file'`.
   119→
   120→**Current Response (`BatchPublishIpnsResponseDto`):**
   121→
   122→```typescript
   123→{
   124→  results: PublishIpnsResponseDto[];
   125→  totalSucceeded: number;
   126→  totalFailed: number;
   127→}
   128→```
   129→
   130→**Rate limits:**
   131→
   132→- Single publish: 10/min/user
   133→- Batch publish: 5/min/user (each batch up to 200 records)
   134→
   135→## Web Client Publish Flow
   136→
   137→### Where Folder Publishes Happen
   138→
   139→Every folder mutation flows through `updateFolderMetadata` in `folder.service.ts`:
   140→
   141→```typescript
   142→export async function updateFolderMetadata(params: {
   143→  folderId: string;
   144→  children: FolderChild[];
   145→  folderKey: Uint8Array;
   146→  ipnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array;
   147→  ipnsName: string;
   148→  sequenceNumber: bigint; // <-- current known sequence
   149→  encryptedIpnsPrivateKey?: string;
   150→  keyEpoch?: number;
   151→}): Promise<{ cid: string; newSequenceNumber: bigint }>;
   152→```
   153→
   154→**Callers of `updateFolderMetadata` (i.e., all folder publish points):**
   155→
   156→1. `useFolderMutations.handleCreate` -- creates subfolder, publishes parent + new folder
   157→2. `useFolderMutations.handleRename` -- renames item, publishes parent via `renameFolder`/`renameFile`
   158→3. `useFolderMutations.handleMove` -- moves item, publishes source and destination
   159→4. `useFolderMutations.handleMoveItems` -- batch move, publishes dest then source
   160→5. `useFolderMutations.handleDelete` -- deletes item, publishes parent via `deleteFolder`/`deleteFileFromFolder`
   161→6. `useFolderMutations.handleDeleteItems` -- batch delete, publishes parent
   162→7. `useFileOperations.handleAddFile` -- uploads file, batch publishes file IPNS + folder via `addFileToFolder`
   163→8. `useFileOperations.handleAddFiles` -- multi-file upload, batch publishes all files + folder via `addFilesToFolder`
   164→9. `useFileOperations.handleUpdateFile` -- updates file content (publishes file IPNS only, NOT folder -- **no conflict check needed**)
   165→10. `checkAndRotateIfNeeded` -- lazy key rotation, publishes folder
   166→
   167→**Batch publish path (`addFileToFolder`, `addFilesToFolder`):**
   168→These use `buildFolderIpnsRecord` + `batchPublishIpnsRecords` instead of `updateFolderMetadata`. The folder record is one entry in the batch alongside file records. Conflict detection must also work here.
   169→
   170→### Sequence Number Tracking in Web Client
   171→
   172→The `FolderNode` in Zustand stores `sequenceNumber: bigint`. Updates:
   173→
   174→- On initial load: from `resolveIpnsRecord` response
   175→- On publish: `updateFolderSequence(parentId, newSequenceNumber)` after publish succeeds
   176→- On sync poll: `updateFolderSequence('root', resolved.sequenceNumber)` after detecting remote changes
   177→
   178→**Important:** Only the root folder is polled for remote changes during sync. Subfolder changes are detected indirectly (root metadata changes -> subfolder metadata is stale).
   179→
   180→## Desktop Client Publish Flow
   181→
   182→### Where Folder Publishes Happen
   183→
   184→Desktop FUSE mutations call `CipherBoxFS::update_folder_metadata(folder_ino)` which calls `spawn_metadata_publish`:
   185→
   186→```rust
   187→fn spawn_metadata_publish(
   188→    api: Arc<ApiClient>,
   189→    rt: tokio::runtime::Handle,
   190→    metadata: FolderMetadata,
   191→    folder_key: Vec<u8>,
   192→    ipns_private_key: Vec<u8>,
   193→    ipns_name: String,
   194→    old_metadata_cid: Option<String>,
   195→    coordinator: Arc<PublishCoordinator>,
   196→)
   197→```
   198→
   199→**Inside `spawn_metadata_publish`:**
   200→
   201→1. Acquire per-folder publish lock (`coordinator.get_lock`)
   202→2. Encrypt metadata (CPU-only)
   203→3. `coordinator.resolve_sequence(api, ipns_name)` -- gets current seq from API
   204→4. Upload encrypted metadata to IPFS
   205→5. Create IPNS record with `new_seq = seq + 1`
   206→6. Call `POST /ipns/publish`
   207→7. `coordinator.record_publish(ipns_name, new_seq)`
   208→
   209→**FUSE write operations that trigger folder publish:**
   210→
   211→- `handle_create` -- new file (via debounce queue)
   212→- `handle_unlink` -- delete file (immediate via `update_folder_metadata`)
   213→- `handle_mkdir` -- new folder (immediate, spawns background thread)
   214→- `handle_rmdir` -- delete folder (immediate via `update_folder_metadata`)
   215→- `handle_rename` -- rename/move (immediate via `update_folder_metadata`)
   216→- `release` -- file upload complete (via debounce queue)
   217→
   218→### PublishCoordinator Details
   219→
   220→```rust
   221→pub struct PublishCoordinator {
   222→    seq_cache: Mutex<HashMap<String, u64>>,      // monotonic local cache
   223→    publish_locks: Mutex<HashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>>, // per-IPNS serialize
   224→}
   225→```
   226→
   227→**`resolve_sequence` behavior:**
   228→
   229→- Calls `resolve_ipns` API -> gets remote seq
   230→- Returns `max(remote_seq, cached_seq)` -- prevents rollback
   231→- On resolve failure with cache hit: returns cached value (fallback)
   232→- On resolve failure without cache: returns error (prevents publishing with unknown seq)
   233→
   234→**The per-folder lock prevents concurrent local publishes** but does NOT prevent conflicts from another device publishing between resolve and publish. This is the exact gap that conflict detection fills.
   235→
   236→## Sync & Polling Mechanism
   237→
   238→### Web Client Sync
   239→
   240→**`useSyncPolling` hook (`useSyncPolling.ts`):**
   241→
   242→- 30s polling interval via `useInterval`
   243→- Pauses when tab is backgrounded or offline
   244→- Fires immediately on mount, visibility regain, and reconnect
   245→- Updates sync store status: idle -> syncing -> success/error
   246→
   247→**Sync callback (`FileBrowser.tsx` lines 116-164):**
   248→
   249→1. Resolve root IPNS name via `resolveIpnsRecord`
   250→2. Compare `resolved.sequenceNumber` with `rootFolder.sequenceNumber`
   251→3. If remote > local: fetch and decrypt new metadata, update store
   252→4. Only polls root folder -- subfolder sync is implicit (root metadata changes reference subfolders)
   253→
   254→**Extension point for conflict re-sync:** The sync callback can be triggered on-demand by calling `doSync()`. After a 409 conflict response, the client could call the sync logic and then retry the operation.
   255→
   256→### Desktop Client Sync
   257→
   258→**`SyncDaemon` (`sync/mod.rs`):**
   259→
   260→- 30s polling interval via tokio timer
   261→- `sync_now_rx` channel for manual triggers (tray "Sync Now" button)
   262→- `poll()`: resolves root IPNS, compares sequence numbers, logs changes
   263→- On change: metadata cache TTL (30s) handles refresh on next FUSE access
   264→- Tray status transitions: Syncing -> Synced / Offline / Error
   265→
   266→**Extension point for conflict re-sync:** The SyncDaemon's `sync_now_rx` channel can trigger immediate re-sync. On conflict, the FUSE publish thread could send to this channel.
   267→
   268→## UI Status Indicators
   269→
   270→### Web - SyncIndicator
   271→
   272→**States (`sync.store.ts`):**
   273→
   274→```typescript
   275→type SyncStatus = 'idle' | 'syncing' | 'success' | 'error';
   276→```
   277→
   278→**Visual (`SyncIndicator.tsx`):**
   279→
   280→- `syncing`: spinning circle icon, "Syncing..."
   281→- `success`: checkmark icon, "Synced"
   282→- `error`: warning icon with exclamation, "Sync failed"
   283→- `idle`: static circle icon, "Sync"
   284→
   285→**Extension needed:** Add a `'conflict'` status (or reuse `'syncing'` during conflict re-sync). A toast notification would be appropriate for the web -- brief, non-blocking, auto-dismissing.
   286→
   287→### Desktop - TrayStatus
   288→
   289→**States (`tray/status.rs`):**
   290→
   291→```rust
   292→enum TrayStatus {
   293→    NotConnected,
   294→    Mounting,
   295→    Syncing,
   296→    Synced,
   297→    Offline,
   298→    Error(String),
   299→}
   300→```
   301→
   302→**Extension needed:** Add `Conflict` variant or use `Error("Conflict: re-syncing...")`. OS notification via `tauri-plugin-notification` (already in `Cargo.toml`).
   303→
   304→## Batch Operations
   305→
   306→### Multi-file Upload
   307→
   308→`addFilesToFolder` creates N file IPNS records + 1 folder IPNS record and sends them all in one `batchPublishIpnsRecords` call. The folder record is the one that needs conflict detection.
   309→
   310→**Important design question:** In a batch publish where individual records can fail independently, should a folder conflict fail the entire batch (preventing the file records from publishing too) or only fail the folder record?
   311→
   312→**Recommendation:** Fail the entire batch when a folder record has a conflict. Reason: the file IPNS records are pointless without the folder record succeeding, because the folder metadata is what makes the files discoverable. Publishing file records but failing the folder record creates orphaned file IPNS records.
   313→
   314→This means: for batch publishes containing a `recordType: 'folder'` entry with `expectedSequenceNumber`, validate the folder entry FIRST. If it conflicts, reject the whole batch with 409.
   315→
   316→### Move Operations
   317→
   318→`handleMove` and `handleMoveItems` publish to two folders sequentially (add-before-remove pattern). If the destination publish succeeds but the source publish conflicts:
   319→
   320→- The item appears in both folders temporarily
   321→- After re-sync, the client sees the conflict on the source folder
   322→- Retry: re-read source folder, remove item, re-publish
   323→- The add-before-remove pattern means data is safe (item exists in at least one folder)
   324→
   325→## Recommendations
   326→
   327→### 1. API Changes
   328→
   329→**Add to `PublishIpnsDto` and `PublishIpnsEntryDto`:**
   330→
   331→```typescript
   332→@IsOptional()
   333→@IsString()
   334→@Matches(/^\d+$/, { message: 'expectedSequenceNumber must be a numeric string' })
   335→expectedSequenceNumber?: string;
   336→```
   337→
   338→**Modify `upsertFolderIpns` in `ipns.service.ts`:**
   339→
   340→```typescript
   341→// Before incrementing sequence_number:
   342→if (expectedSequenceNumber !== undefined && existing) {
   343→  const expected = BigInt(expectedSequenceNumber);
   344→  const current = BigInt(existing.sequenceNumber);
   345→  if (expected !== current) {
   346→    throw new ConflictException({
   347→      message: 'Sequence number mismatch',
   348→      currentSequenceNumber: existing.sequenceNumber,
   349→      expectedSequenceNumber: expectedSequenceNumber,
   350→    });
   351→  }
   352→}
   353→```
   354→
   355→**HTTP response:** 409 Conflict with body:
   356→
   357→```json
   358→{
   359→  "statusCode": 409,
   360→  "message": "Sequence number mismatch",
   361→  "currentSequenceNumber": "5",
   362→  "expectedSequenceNumber": "3"
   363→}
   364→```
   365→
   366→**Batch publish behavior:** When processing batch records, if ANY folder-type record with `expectedSequenceNumber` conflicts, stop processing and return 409 for the entire batch. File-type records do not use `expectedSequenceNumber`.
   367→
   368→### 2. Web Client Changes
   369→
   370→**In `updateFolderMetadata`:** Pass the current `sequenceNumber` as `expectedSequenceNumber` in the publish request.
   371→
   372→**In `createAndPublishIpnsRecord`:** Accept and forward `expectedSequenceNumber` to the API call.
   373→
   374→**Conflict handling (in each hook that calls `updateFolderMetadata`):**
   375→
   376→```typescript
   377→try {
   378→  await folderService.updateFolderMetadata({...});
   379→} catch (err) {
   380→  if (isConflictError(err)) {
   381→    // 1. Show toast: "Folder updated by another device, re-syncing..."
   382→    // 2. Re-sync: resolve IPNS, fetch & decrypt metadata, update store
   383→    // 3. Re-read fresh folder state from store
   384→    // 4. Re-apply the user's operation on the fresh state
   385→    // 5. Retry publish with fresh sequence number
   386→  }
   387→  throw err;
   388→}
   389→```
   390→
   391→**Retry strategy:** Single retry after re-sync. If the retry also conflicts (highly unlikely), surface error to user. No infinite retry loops.
   392→
   393→**Toast notification style:** Inline toast at the bottom of the file browser, auto-dismiss after 5 seconds. States: "Re-syncing..." (spinner), "Synced - operation completed" (checkmark), or "Conflict persists - please try again" (warning).
   394→
   395→### 3. Desktop Client Changes
   396→
   397→**In `spawn_metadata_publish`:** After `coordinator.resolve_sequence`, pass the resolved sequence as `expectedSequenceNumber` in the publish request.

   441→## Common Pitfalls
   442→
   443→### Pitfall 1: Race Between Resolve and Publish
   444→
   445→**What goes wrong:** Client resolves seq=5, another device publishes (seq becomes 6), client publishes with expectedSeq=5, gets 409.
   446→**Why it happens:** Normal multi-device usage. The resolve-then-publish pattern has an inherent TOCTOU window.
   447→**How to avoid:** This is expected behavior -- the conflict detection is designed to catch this. The client's response (re-sync + retry) handles it.
   448→
   449→### Pitfall 2: Stale Zustand Closures in Retry Logic
   450→
   451→**What goes wrong:** The retry callback uses the original `parentFolderState` from the closure, which has the stale sequence number and children.
   452→**Why it happens:** React hook callbacks capture state at render time.
   453→**How to avoid:** In retry logic, ALWAYS re-read from `useFolderStore.getState()` to get fresh folder state. This is a known pattern in this codebase (see MEMORY.md "Zustand stale closures in async callbacks").
   454→
   455→### Pitfall 3: Infinite Retry on Persistent Conflict
   456→
   457→**What goes wrong:** Two devices in a tight loop modifying the same folder cause infinite conflict retries.
   458→**Why it happens:** Each retry triggers a new publish which conflicts with the other device's retry.
   459→**How to avoid:** Limit to 1 retry per operation. If the retry also conflicts, surface an error to the user. Consider adding random jitter (100-500ms) before retry to break symmetry.
   460→
   461→### Pitfall 4: Batch Publish Partial Conflict
   462→
   463→**What goes wrong:** In a batch with 10 file records + 1 folder record, the folder conflicts but file records have already been processed.
   464→**Why it happens:** Current batch processing runs records concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.
   465→**How to avoid:** For batches containing a folder record with `expectedSequenceNumber`, validate the folder record FIRST. If it conflicts, return 409 for the entire batch before processing any records.
   466→
   467→### Pitfall 5: Move Operation Half-Conflict
   468→
   469→**What goes wrong:** Destination publish succeeds, source publish gets 409. Item exists in both folders.
   470→**Why it happens:** Move is two separate publish operations (add-before-remove).
   471→**How to avoid:** This is actually safe due to add-before-remove pattern. On source conflict: re-sync source folder, re-verify item is still in source children, re-publish removal. The item temporarily appears in both folders but data is not lost.
   472→
   473→### Pitfall 6: Desktop Publish Lock Does Not Prevent Remote Conflicts
   474→
   475→**What goes wrong:** Developer assumes `PublishCoordinator.get_lock` prevents all conflicts.
   476→**Why it happens:** The lock only serializes local publishes from the same desktop process.
   477→**How to avoid:** The lock is necessary (prevents local race conditions) but not sufficient (does not prevent remote device conflicts). Both the local lock AND the API-level conflict check are needed.
   478→
   479→### Pitfall 7: Conflict During Lazy Key Rotation
   480→
   481→**What goes wrong:** `checkAndRotateIfNeeded` publishes re-encrypted metadata, but another device published since the last sync.
   482→**Why it happens:** Key rotation resolves IPNS, re-encrypts, publishes -- standard TOCTOU window.
   483→**How to avoid:** Key rotation publish should also use `expectedSequenceNumber`. On conflict, re-sync, re-read metadata, and re-encrypt with the new key using the fresh children.
   484→
   485→## Don't Hand-Roll
   486→
   487→| Problem                     | Don't Build                | Use Instead                          | Why                                                                                     |
   488→| --------------------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   489→| Conflict detection protocol | Custom distributed locking | HTTP 409 + `expectedSequenceNumber`  | Standard optimistic concurrency pattern; proven at scale                                |
   490→| OS notifications on desktop | Custom notification system | `tauri-plugin-notification`          | Already a dependency, handles macOS/Windows/Linux                                       |
   491→| Web toast notifications     | Custom toast from scratch  | Simple CSS transition + `setTimeout` | The existing codebase uses inline components, not a toast library; keep it consistent   |
   492→| Retry backoff               | Custom exponential backoff | Single retry with random jitter      | Conflicts are rare (30s poll interval >> publish duration); complex backoff is overkill |
   493→

   532→export function isConflictError(error: unknown): error is Error & {
   533→  status: number;
   534→  body: { currentSequenceNumber: string };

   542→### Desktop: Conflict Error Detection
   543→
   544→```rust
   545→// In api/ipns.rs, modify publish_ipns return type:
   546→pub enum PublishResult {
   547→    Success,
   548→    Conflict { current_sequence_number: String },
   549→}
   550→
   551→pub async fn publish_ipns(
   552→    client: &ApiClient,
   553→    request: &IpnsPublishRequest,
   554→) -> Result<PublishResult, String> {
   555→    let resp = client.authenticated_post("/ipns/publish", request).await

   562→            .as_str()
   563→            .unwrap_or("0")
   564→            .to_string();
   565→        return Ok(PublishResult::Conflict {
   566→            current_sequence_number: current_seq
   567→        });
   568→    }

   573→## Risk Assessment
   574→
   575→### Low Risk
   576→
   577→- **API DTO change:** Adding an optional field is backward-compatible
   578→- **409 response code:** Standard HTTP semantics, well-understood
   579→- **Web toast notification:** Simple UI addition, no complex state
   580→
   581→### Medium Risk
   582→
   583→- **Batch publish conflict handling:** Need to restructure batch processing to validate folder records first. Current `Promise.allSettled` concurrent processing must be changed to sequential for folder records with conflict checks.
   584→- **Desktop conflict retry in FUSE context:** The FUSE callback thread spawns a background publish thread. On conflict, the retry must re-read inode state which may have changed. Need careful locking.
   585→- **Move operation half-conflict:** Safe due to add-before-remove, but the retry logic for the source removal needs to handle the case where the item was already removed by the other device's sync.
   586→
   587→### Low Probability but High Impact
   588→
   589→- **TypeORM race condition:** Two publish requests arriving simultaneously could both read the same `sequenceNumber` before either writes. Using a DB-level `WHERE sequence_number = expected` in the UPDATE query (instead of read-then-compare) would be more robust. Consider using TypeORM's query builder with a conditional update.
   590→
   591→## Open Questions
   592→
   593→1. **DB-level vs application-level check:**
   594→   - Current plan: read record, compare in TypeScript, then update
   595→   - More robust: `UPDATE folder_ipns SET sequence_number = seq + 1 WHERE sequence_number = expected RETURNING *`
   596→   - Recommendation: Use DB-level `WHERE` clause for atomicity. The application-level read-compare-write has a TOCTOU gap under high concurrency.
   597→   - **Confidence:** MEDIUM -- need to verify TypeORM supports conditional updates well
   598→
   599→2. **Should subfolder sync be added?**
   600→   - Currently only root folder is polled on web. If a conflict occurs on a subfolder, the client needs to re-sync that specific subfolder.
   601→   - Recommendation: On conflict, resolve the specific folder's IPNS (not just root), fetch and decrypt, update store. This is already how `loadFolder` works.
   602→   - **Confidence:** HIGH -- the resolve infrastructure exists
   603→
   604→3. **TEE republish interaction:**
   605→   - TEE republishes use `sequence_number` from the `republish_schedules` table. TEE does NOT use `expectedSequenceNumber`.
   606→   - Does a TEE republish increment the `folder_ipns.sequence_number`? Looking at the code, TEE publishes go through the same `upsertFolderIpns` path, which increments unconditionally.
   607→   - This means a TEE republish could cause a client conflict even though the content hasn't changed (same CID, just refreshed IPNS TTL).
   608→   - Recommendation: Only set `expectedSequenceNumber` on client publishes. TEE republishes continue without it. The DB sequence will still increment on TEE republish, but since TEE uses the same CID, the client's next sync will see a higher sequence number with identical content -- triggering a no-op refresh.
   609→   - **Confidence:** HIGH -- TEE publish path already uses the same upsert without expected seq
